jokes.explanation: The episode's best joke. The structure is perfect: Jeff starts with 'I'm not just a pretty face that murders people' (already great), then self-corrects to 'I'm less than that — I'm a gorgeous face.' The correction UPGRADES 'pretty' to 'gorgeous' while DOWNGRADING the expectation. It's simultaneously self-deprecating and vain, sincere and shallow. Perfectly in character — Jeff's narcissism is physically incapable of letting 'pretty' stand when 'gorgeous' is available. This is a 9+ joke. Very high craft, very quotable, could only come from Jeff.

jokes.text: 'Now, to be fair, you guys know Willy's an innocent man, right?' / 'You shut your mouth, Warden!' — reveal of Willy's innocence
jokes.setup: Everyone has been treating Willy as a confirmed murderer throughout the episode
jokes.punchline: He's actually wrongfully convicted — the reveal recontextualizes the entire episode and Jeff's 'I try to reserve strong feelings for myself' dark-comedy thread
jokes.explanation: Good structural comedy — the entire episode's dark-comedy murder thread is retroactively reframed. 'You shut your mouth, Warden!' from Jeff is a funny reaction to learning your enemy is actually innocent. The misdirection is well-executed over the whole episode.

jokes.text: 'You're... not a murderer?' / 'I can explain.' / 'Oh, how the mighty have fallen. You son of a bitch!'
jokes.setup: Jeff discovers Willy is innocent
jokes.punchline: Jeff's 'Oh, how the mighty have fallen. You son of a bitch!' — his anger is not at the false murder accusation but at the LOSS OF COOL that comes from not being a murderer
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. Jeff's fury is 100% about Willy losing his murderer cachet, not about being manipulated or endangered. 'How the mighty have fallen' applied to the revelation of innocence is a perfect inversion. The 'you son of a bitch!' as a kicker is very funny — the indignation is completely misdirected. High originality, great structure.

jokes.text: 'Wait, let's do this by community college rules. Fight! Fight! Fight!'
jokes.setup: Jeff says 'let's do this by prison rules' and attacks Willy
jokes.punchline: Annie counter-proposes 'community college rules' — which apparently means everyone chants 'Fight! Fight! Fight!'
jokes.explanation: Annie immediately abandoning her rules persona to chant for a fight is a great character subversion. 'Community college rules' as its own formal alternative to 'prison rules' is a funny concept.

jokes.text: Jeff vs. Willy's robot — physical fight between human and telepresence robot, 'Go, brooms, go!' and 'You punch like a girl!'
jokes.setup: Jeff is fighting a robot
jokes.punchline: The visual absurdity of a human fistfighting a telepresence robot — especially 'You punch like a girl!' (from a machine)
jokes.explanation: Physical comedy that likely plays very well on screen. The absurdity of a human fighting a robot piloted by a prisoner hundreds of miles away is rich, and 'You punch like a girl!' from an iPad on a stick is funny. Impact score reflects the visual comedy value.

jokes.text: 'What the hell kind of school is this?' — the Warden's bewildered reaction after witnessing the entire episode's chaos
jokes.setup: The Warden has just witnessed a ceremony turn into a Dean/prisoner love declaration, a robot fight, and general chaos
jokes.punchline: His completely reasonable question serves as the audience surrogate moment — asking what any new viewer would ask
jokes.explanation: Functional audience-surrogate joke. The punchline is obvious but earned by everything preceding it. 'What the hell kind of school is this?' captures the episode's chaos neatly.

jokes.text: Telepresence robot meeting chaos: Britta appearing to be arrested, Chang calling from what sounds like someone else's bathroom, 'Please tell me you're not doing the thing I think you're doing. Ew.'
jokes.setup: The group is trying to have a meeting via the purchased telepresence robots
jokes.punchline: Multiple simultaneous disasters: Britta is apparently being arrested, Chang is definitely in someone else's bathroom based on the tile matching the apartment
jokes.explanation: Great escalating chaos sequence. The Chang bathroom callback (the same tile as the apartment bathroom) is a clever visual callback — someone finally identifies whose bathroom he's been using. 'Please tell me you're not doing the thing I think you're doing' is very funny in context. The simultaneous chaos across multiple robot screens works well as an ending gag.

jokes.text: It's hard to tell without side cameras. / Wait, why am I moving? Is my custom background working?
jokes.setup: The group is meeting via telepresence robots to debrief
jokes.punchline: Characters are struggling with their own robot controls and custom backgrounds — 'it's hard to tell without side cameras' and the moving robot are meta-comments on the absurdity of communicating this way
jokes.explanation: The group robot meeting is a good comedic payoff to the episode's premise — now everyone is using the technology. The technical chaos (custom backgrounds, involuntary movement) reflects how quickly tech creates new social awkwardness. Decent but not exceptional.

jokes.text: As you've heard, the rehabilitation program has been aborted, so we lost that money. But we no longer have to build 67 ramps, so we should break even.
jokes.setup: The program has failed; the school has lost $300,000
jokes.punchline: Frankie's pragmatic accounting — 67 unbuilt ramps save enough money to break even — is funny in its bureaucratic precision. '67 ramps' is a very specific number that suggests real calculations were done
jokes.explanation: '67 ramps' is a perfect Frankie detail — specific enough to be funny, implying she's done the actual math. The deadpan 'so we should break even' as the resolution to a catastrophic failure is very Frankie. Good character integration.

jokes.text: I gotta go! / Oh, my God. / Yeah, I gotta go too. Oh, Jeffrey! / I take it we're passing on their offer. / No, they're just amateurs. Initiating override protocol.
jokes.setup: Everyone is fleeing the robot meeting after Chang's bathroom revelation
jokes.punchline: Abed's 'No, they're just amateurs. Initiating override protocol' — coolly taking control of all the robots after everyone else panics — sets up the Dalek finale
jokes.explanation: Abed's calm takeover — 'they're just amateurs' — is a great character beat. His matter-of-fact competence in a chaos situation is funny. 'Override protocol' implies Abed has been waiting for this opportunity. Good setup for the closing gag.

jokes.text: 'Abeds, commence with world domination. Eradicate. Eradicate! Eradicate! Eradicate.'
jokes.setup: The meeting ends with a vote to purchase the telepresence robots
jokes.punchline: Abed, now controlling multiple robots, channels a Dalek ('Eradicate! Eradicate!') — a sci-fi villain reference suggesting he's been waiting for robot domination all along
jokes.explanation: Perfect episode-ending joke — Abed has been patient all episode and now gets his robot army. The Dalek 'Eradicate!' reference is perfect Abed character work: a sci-fi parody of world domination fantasy. 'Abeds, commence' (plural) suggests there are multiple Abed robots, which is a funny escalation. Great final note.

tmdb_overview: When prisoners roll into Greendale via telerobot, Jeff meets his match in a clever convict. Britta's plans for a raging house party backfire.
insight: Season 6's weakest episode: 82 jokes at 2.94/min yield just 68.4 impact.
